newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First's Peters reassures financial markets.
newsitem.headline: NZ First's Peters reassures financial markets.

text.p: New Zealand First Party leader Winston Peters told financial markets on Saturday his party was committed to sound economic policies as it exercised the balance of power in a general election.

"We in New Zealand First are committed to expanding New Zealand's trading base, to running budget surpluses, repaying debt and rewarding the hard work enterprise of our citizens," Peters told supporters.
Peters declined to spell out his bottom line in negotiations in response to reporters' questions.
"Nothing more can be progressed tonight," he said. He expected to speak to both Labour leader Helen Clark and National Party leader Jim Bolger within the next 48 hours.
Peters called for patience as coalition talks began.

Latest TV1 projections give the conservative National Party about 45 seats in the new parliament, Labour 36, New Zealand First 17, the left-wing Alliance 13, radical free-market Act eight and centrist United one.
